title: Assist on a held-up page
description: Start or end your assist on a page another owner holds (the person, another agent, the Chat bot, a workflow run) while its work is held up (dsagent.monitor.snapshot: blocked, assist available).
guidance: While it lasts (5 minutes; start again to renew) your dsagent.page.action / actions / focus are admitted there although the page is not yours; the page stays its owner's. Walls stay decided as on your own pages: a verification challenge is yours to pass under its attempt budget while the person's Verification Challenges switch is on, a sign-in wall is never yours. When the page is clear, end the assist: if the wall is verified gone, the task or run that waited on it continues. An assist ends by itself once nothing holds the page up any more (refused then with MONITOR_ASSIST_ENDED), when it lapses, when your connection ends or when the person turns the monitor off. Refusals: ASSIST_NOT_NEEDED (act directly), NOT_BLOCKED (its owner works; leave it), ASSIST_HELD (another agent assists), MONITOR_OFF. Requires an idempotency key.

inputSchema.description: Which page, and start or end.

operation.description: start (or renew) your assist, or end it.

state.description: assisting: act on the page now; ended: the assist is over.

attention.description: What holds the work up, each with who must act. Empty when nothing does.

code.description: sign-in-wall: a sign-in, one-time-code, consent or block page that only the person can pass; verification-challenge: a CAPTCHA, slider, picture or bot check an agent may pass with page actions (dsagent.page.action under its challenge budget, while the person's Verification Challenges switch is on); waiting-for-answer: a task waits for the person's answer to its question; paused-for-repair: a run waits for the repair of a failed block (dsagent.execution.handoff.*, only its starting agent answers); paused-for-resources: a run waits for host memory or CPU; task-failed / task-interrupted / run-failed: the work ended without its result; stalled: a running task published no step (and, an outside agent's task, made no MCP call) for 3 minutes (reported only, it stays its owner's).

waitingOn.description: Who must act for it to clear: the person, an agent (the owner, or one assisting), or nobody (the work ended; report it).

since.description: Since when (ISO 8601), when the owner says.

detail.description: A typed, value-free detail: the wall type, the run endpoint, the failure code.

task.description: One task running (or just ended) in the browser.

taskRef.description: Opaque, stable reference of the task.

kind.description: An outside agent's task (its connection to DSphere), a DSphere Chat bot task, or a workflow run (started by the person, a schedule, the Chat bot or an agent).

mine.description: Your own task, or a run you started.

ownerName.description: The outside agent that owns the task or started the run, when one did.

description.description: The task as its owner described it (an agent's taskDescription, the Chat request), or the run's workflow name.

status.description: Its owner's status: a Chat or agent task phase (planning, acting, paused-auth, awaiting-user, failed…), a run status (running, paused-auth-interrupt, paused-agent-repair, failed…), or running / ended for an agent connection.

lastActivityAt.description: Its last published step, or for an outside agent's task its last MCP call if later (ISO 8601).

partOfTaskRef.description: A workflow run started (or read) by an outside agent for one of its tasks: the taskRef of that agent task, listed beside it. The run keeps its own row and events; read the two as one task of the agent.

pageContextIds.description: The task's open pages; empty for a run whose tab is gone, or for an agent task whose pages are closed while it still works (or just ended).

attention.description: What holds the work up, each with who must act. Empty when nothing does.

code.description: sign-in-wall: a sign-in, one-time-code, consent or block page that only the person can pass; verification-challenge: a CAPTCHA, slider, picture or bot check an agent may pass with page actions (dsagent.page.action under its challenge budget, while the person's Verification Challenges switch is on); waiting-for-answer: a task waits for the person's answer to its question; paused-for-repair: a run waits for the repair of a failed block (dsagent.execution.handoff.*, only its starting agent answers); paused-for-resources: a run waits for host memory or CPU; task-failed / task-interrupted / run-failed: the work ended without its result; stalled: a running task published no step (and, an outside agent's task, made no MCP call) for 3 minutes (reported only, it stays its owner's).

waitingOn.description: Who must act for it to clear: the person, an agent (the owner, or one assisting), or nobody (the work ended; report it).

since.description: Since when (ISO 8601), when the owner says.

detail.description: A typed, value-free detail: the wall type, the run endpoint, the failure code.

siteResponsiveness.description: Present only while something is wrong with how websites answer this task's tab; absent when they answer normally. site-slow: the website itself is slow, stalled, failing, rate-limiting or unreachable while other websites in the same tab answer normally, so it is not a browser or Agent fault. local-network-slow: every website is slow alike, so it is the person's network or proxy. Either way: do not switch browsers, reload the extension or repeat actions faster; tell the person once which website is slow, then wait (dsagent_page_wait) and read again. DSphere never changes its own timeouts because of it.

verdict.description: site-slow: the website is the problem; local-network-slow: the person's network or proxy is.

reason.description: What is wrong: slow answers (median wait 3 s or more), requests waiting over 10 s, failing requests (5xx or connection errors), rate limiting (HTTP 429), or the website cannot be reached.

host.description: Host name of the tab's website; never a path or query.

medianWaitMs.description: Median time the website took to start answering over the last 20 s; absent when no request answered.

stalledRequests.description: The website's requests waiting more than 10 s without an answer (long polls excluded).

failedRequests.description: The website's requests that failed in the last 20 s.

sampledRequests.description: The website's requests counted in the last 20 s.

controlMedianWaitMs.description: Median wait of the other websites the same tab loaded over the last 60 s (the comparison); absent when none answered.

hint.description: One sentence on what to do.

wallCleared.description: With ended: whether a fresh read found the page without a wall; absent when that read could not check the page (its content did not answer), and then the paused owner stays paused.

ownerResumed.description: With ended: the task or run that waited on the wall continues.
